key_insight: A physics-based reduced-order model combines meniscus curvature, viscous losses and contact-line hysteresis to predict dissipative low-gravity sloshing.
engineering_relevance: Faster-than-real-time simulation of coupled spacecraft translation and sloshing can support control analyses that account for uncertain damping.
method: Represent curved-meniscus inertia and restoring forces with Dirichlet–Neumann and Jacobi operators.
Combine bulk, Stokes-layer and contact-line dissipation in a passive port-Hamiltonian formulation.
Propagate analytically between contact-line stick–slip events.
evidence_signal: Across 42 drop-tower and ground measurements, curvature correction reduced RMS frequency error from 24% to 4%; one calibrated hysteresis width predicted additional MODE tests with 11–35% normalized force errors.
watch_item: Uncertain wetting and remaining response discrepancies warrant damping ranges rather than a single nominal value in spacecraft control studies.
paper_title: A curvature-corrected port-Hamiltonian reduced-order model for dissipative sloshing with contact-line hysteresis in low-gravity tanks
